## Database gate
- Database structure and embedded SQL changed. The earlier automatic conflict report stopped before database analysis; this review supersedes that incomplete result.
- Official `251_group_force_openai_ultrafast.sql` adds `groups.force_openai_ultrafast BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`; the disabled default preserves existing groups. Ent schema, generated fields, repository projections, DTOs, cache and group cloning must carry the new value.
- Official `251_group_usage_rollup_nonblocking_build.sql` adds `expired_before`, `building_until` and `build_dirty_from` to `usage_group_rollup_state`, and replaces four invalidation functions. The expired floor defaults to the Unix epoch; build markers are nullable. Review covers dirty-date watermarks, timezone conversion and `FOR KEY SHARE` versus build-registration/publication locks. Its transaction sets `lock_timeout=5s`; lock failure must abort migration and startup.
- Both migrations retain exact official blobs. Their shared numeric prefix is accepted because the unchanged runner sorts and records complete filenames, validates checksums and holds its existing advisory lock. Do not rename or renumber released SQL.
- Official embedded SQL changes include same-user atomic batch billing, request-fingerprint deduplication, sorted row-lock acquisition, group rollup publication/retention and user-group rate overrides. Custom schema exceptions are re-bound to the new official commit and exact regenerated candidate blobs; no unrelated database feature is introduced.
- Batch subscription billing calls `incrementUsageBillingSubscription`, which still invokes `subscriptionquota.IncrementCycleUsageTx` in the same SQL transaction. Duplicate claims and failed batches must not increase cycle usage. The trusted Linux Integration run validates the application against disposable PostgreSQL/Redis; it is not a production database backup or a production-data rehearsal.

### Read-only production checks (not executed)

```sql
BEGIN READ ONLY;
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
  AND ((table_name = 'groups' AND column_name = 'force_openai_ultrafast')
    OR (table_name = 'usage_group_rollup_state'
      AND column_name IN ('expired_before', 'building_until', 'build_dirty_from')))
ORDER BY table_name, column_name;
SELECT filename, checksum FROM schema_migrations
WHERE filename IN ('251_group_force_openai_ultrafast.sql',
                   '251_group_usage_rollup_nonblocking_build.sql')
ORDER BY filename;
SELECT p.proname, pg_get_functiondef(p.oid)
FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace
WHERE n.nspname = current_schema()
  AND p.proname IN ('apply_group_usage_rollup_invalidation',
    'invalidate_group_usage_rollups_at', 'invalidate_group_usage_rollup_state',
    'invalidate_group_usage_rollup_state_after_insert');
COMMIT;
```

### Forward migration, backup and rollback

- The two official SQL files are the reviewed forward migration SQL, including idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` and `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`. No additional hand-written production migration is necessary. A future application startup will run pending migrations; building or publishing this release does not execute them. No production SQL, real payment, production deployment or backup was executed by this upgrade task.
- Before deploying, require a verified PostgreSQL backup containing `groups`, `usage_logs`, `usage_group_daily_rollups`, `usage_group_rollup_state`, `user_subscriptions`, `user_subscription_cycles`, billing dedup tables and `schema_migrations`; retain v0.2.21-custom.1 binaries, manifest and OCI digest. Restore the backup into an isolated copy and verify both complete migration filenames and the read-only checks before production startup.
- DDL takes table locks despite additive columns; plan a low-traffic window and treat the 5-second lock timeout as a deployment failure. Test concurrent historical INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and rollup rebuilds in the isolated database; successful CI is schema-level evidence, not proof of production lock duration.
- Program rollback alone cannot reverse replaced PL/pgSQL functions, watermarks or newly applied migration records. Stop writers first and restore the matching pre-upgrade database snapshot plus previous trusted runtime/image when a full rollback is required; never drop columns or delete migration records as an automatic rollback. Any post-backup traffic must be reconciled before restore.
